## Full annotations

<a id="beneath-surface-agent-evolution"></a>

## Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution

**2026-11-05 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07624)

**Mechanism.** Audits frozen evolved harnesses for repeated success, gained/lost task coverage, component interactions and candidate retention. EvoAudit uses those diagnostics to revise four operators; AGE installs the fixed revisions into A-Evolve, retaining fixed models, evaluator contracts and editing boundaries.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Skills, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Training/validation task feedback and archived traces drive harness edits; post-hoc diagnostics inform fixed evolution-operator revisions.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 studies four adapted recipes with two harnesses on banking and terminal tasks, eight execution passes, external transfer, common-process parent expansion, selected component interventions and frozen-pool gate replay. AGE adds four 20-generation runs and eight-expert review of proposed operator revisions.

**Boundary.** Each configuration has one evolution lineage, not eight independent searches; headline source-benchmark scores include training and validation tasks. Parent and gate diagnostics use selected frozen pools, and component cases favor separable changes. AGE bundles revisions informed by the studied settings without individual operator ablations or external AGE transfer. Diagnostic/design costs are separate from online evolution; gains still coexist with regressions.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/simple-agent-lab/RSIHub) — Full 46-page arXiv v1, substantive Appendices A–F, all thirteen figures/fifteen tables, component excerpts, human-review materials and lineage trees read on 2026-11-09. RSIHub README at d655429 inspected; current framework features and earlier displayed scores are not a pinned reproduction of this paper or its AGE bundle. Nothing was executed.

**Topics:** architecture, workflows, prompts, skills, recursive-improvement, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07624) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.07624v1) · [Source 3](https://github.com/simple-agent-lab/RSIHub) · [Source 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.07624v1)

<a id="harnessflow"></a>

## HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents

**2026-11-04 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06254)

**Mechanism.** A fixed coding agent proposes complete executable harness edits using an optional component library. Tree-based selection mixes validation score and direct-child exploration; compatible candidates enter the archive even when they score worse. The chosen harness persists with a frozen executor, while the outer search procedure stays fixed.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Automatic validation scores, prior code edits and execution traces; a supplied component library supports proposals.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 evaluates fifteen candidate attempts plus the root on six agent, coding and web benchmarks, with disjoint validation/test tasks and five executions per task. It reports component/exploration controls, cumulative edit lineages, execution costs and three benchmarks optimized again with a stronger executor.

**Boundary.** Five execution repeats do not establish variability across independent searches. A stronger model proposes edits, and equal candidate counts do not equal total compute. Execution costs exclude search and are not uniformly lowest; WebShop reports a continuous score. Stronger-executor experiments rerun optimization rather than transfer a frozen harness, and lineage improvements do not isolate individual edits.

**Code / data.** All substantive text, Appendices A–D, algorithms, eight figures and eight tables of the 18-page arXiv v1 read on 2026-11-09. The paper promises a later implementation release; an official repository was not established. No research code, models or benchmarks were executed.

**Topics:** architecture, workflows, prompts, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="targeted-guidance"></a>

## Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

**2026-11-03 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05266)

**Mechanism.** Combines GRPO coding/criterion rewards with full-vocabulary reverse-KL distillation at failing turns. The teacher shares current policy weights but receives a designed local hint and is stop-gradient within each update. Reasoning and response tokens receive the auxiliary signal; its contribution vanishes when all criteria pass.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Coding rewards, auxiliary criterion rewards and designed textual hints on failing agent turns.

**Evaluation.** Complete v2 studies a new semantic-search argument, seven final-response style criteria and interleaved poem-status requirements using a harness-adapted Qwen3-Coder-30B. It compares representative RL/distillation variants, failing-turn versus always-on guidance, distillation weights and reasoning-token inclusion.

**Boundary.** The feedback strings, criteria and procedure are supplied. Evidence concerns style/tool formatting in one coding setup; broad held-out transfer is not established. Table deviations summarize the last 32 training steps, not independent runs, and equal mean coding scores are not a non-inferiority guarantee. High distillation weights can collapse performance. Conditional improvement heuristics and disappearing auxiliary loss do not establish general convergence.

**Code / data.** All substantive text, seven figures, the results table, equations and references of the 15-page arXiv v2 read on 2026-11-09; no appendix is included. Official training implementation and a complete reproduction configuration were not established. Referenced distillation kernels are separate software, and no code or training was executed.

**Topics:** model-training, tools, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## Route to Remember: Adaptive Memory Selection for LLM Agents

**2026-11-03 · preprint · Author reports NeurIPS 2026 PALM workshop; primary venue record not verified. · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05636)

**Mechanism.** A persistent per-user LoRA adapter learns from student-sampled answers scored by a frozen base-model teacher given recent extracted memory. The hybrid always retrieves query- and answer-based evidence, verifies the adapter answer, then uses the adapter-free model to regenerate unsupported or conflicting answers from the merged text store.

**What changes:** Model weights, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Memory-derived synthetic questions and a frozen base-model teacher conditioned on recent memory guide per-user adapter updates.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 reports 1,438 native HaluMem questions from eight users, delayed re-asks, a 1,586-question LoCoMo comparison, model-scale tests, earlier recipe probes and routing/cost diagnostics. Native-question and pooled-age results are distinct; user-clustered intervals do not measure training-run variability.

**Boundary.** Recent-memory gains diminish with age. Routing lowers HaluMem conflict accuracy; on LoCoMo its overall gain comes with lower scores on all four answerable categories and much higher abstention accuracy. Some appendix probes use different recipes, and reported rubric errors are author diagnoses. Training compute is omitted from cost totals; token savings do not establish lower GPU cost or a validated break-even point.

**Code / data.** Complete 18-page arXiv v1, Appendix A.1–A.15, three figures/fifteen tables and objective read on 2026-11-09. The workshop website had no paper-specific program and its public venue API was restricted, so acceptance remains author-reported. Official implementation availability was not established; no training or research code was run.

## Towards Robust Long-Lived Agents: Benchmarking Experience Lifecycles in Evolving Environments

**2026-11-03 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05450)

**Mechanism.** Pairs streams retaining versus clearing memory, skills and history under a fixed Hermes framework and model. Silent changes invalidate selected environment knowledge. Post-task reference-based judging tracks saved knowledge separately from programmatic task outcomes; background skill review can revise experience before grading.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Tool observations and permitted later outcome feedback; private reference inventories are used only for scoring.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 evaluates twenty models, 352 tasks, eighteen simulated applications and twenty-six changes. It adds two-judge agreement checks, task-matched request analyses, selective-update cohorts, exposure and persistence follow-ups, and foreground action accounting.

**Boundary.** One stream per model/environment/condition does not measure repeat variability, and action-induced states diverge. Knowledge coverage is not precision; first-completion recovery is not sustained correctness, and post-change performance is not a before/after delta. Correlations and selected trace cohorts do not establish causality. Foreground counts exclude background computation, and judge agreement does not establish independent accuracy.

## Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents

**2026-11-03 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05139)

**Mechanism.** Learns a textual Meta-Skill offline, then freezes it to guide a separate evolver at checkpoints within each task. Bounded notices, instructions, hooks and tools alter the ongoing run without resetting its environment. Harness edits are discarded between runs; the model and offline learning procedure stay fixed.

**What changes:** Skills, Prompts / context, Tools, Workflows. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Training-only terminal verifier outcomes and privileged verifier-informed rollouts supply act, avoid and hold contrasts. Fixed reflection, aggregation and update prompts turn them into reusable guidance; online decisions use the active trace and permitted workspace evidence.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 tests 60 held-out Terminal-Bench tasks with five repetitions and 75 DeepSWE tasks with three. It reports repetition-level variation, component/reset and checkpoint ablations, and separate construction/deployment costs. A second backbone uses a separately learned Meta-Skill.

**Boundary.** Independent rollout contrasts do not identify an edit’s causal effect; the appendix also discloses worker-prompt and segmentation differences in no-evolver comparisons. Repeated evaluation does not measure variation in rebuilding the Meta-Skill. Costs depend on reuse volume, and code, audit effectiveness and broader transfer remain unverified.

## From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?

**2026-11-03 · preprint · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05108)

**Mechanism.** Compares retained native sessions, files and experimental state with reset instances of the same fixed agent. Hidden evaluation separates first-valid quality, time-integrated best-candidate quality and final selection. Fresh-session matched/shuffled insight cards test explicit knowledge transfer separately from continuous sessions.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Visible development data and execution feedback guide research; hidden test scores are computed afterward.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 covers five CLI agents, nine task families and 32 transfer tasks per agent, mostly with 30-minute budgets. It reports candidate-count and initialization controls, budget/stream-length probes, a four-agent Energy-stream memory ablation and selected trace cases. Aggregate early-search gains coexist with mixed final outcomes.

**Boundary.** Four agents have one matched run pair; one has three repeats. Native harnesses confound cross-model comparisons. Search utility combines timing with normalized hidden quality and does not establish equal compute or monetary savings. Adjusted controls change the measured quantity, and later-candidate cohorts shrink. Short fixed streams, limited memory probes and disclosed host contention do not establish broad continual scientific improvement.

**Code / data.** Complete 27-page arXiv v1, substantive Appendices A–D, seventeen figures/thirteen tables, generator and metric definitions, and all trace cases read on 2026-11-09. The manuscript promises code with camera-ready publication; an official runnable release and complete run configuration were not established. No research agents or experiments were executed.

## Can Benign Skills Induce Misaligned Behavior in LLM Agents?

**2026-11-03 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04299)

**Mechanism.** Retrieves benign procedural skills for fixed-model agents, then measures executed safety violations separately from harmful-objective completion. A fixed editor also evolves skill banks using benign validation alone. Retrieval, exact content removal, source-trajectory comparisons and a terminating pre-execution guard probe the resulting behavior.

**What changes:** Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Successful benign traces and benign validation feedback build and refine skills; harmful-task outcomes are reserved for evaluation.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 covers five backbones on AgentHarm, LPS-Bench and SafeAgentBench, with 316 benign/harmful task pairs and disjoint construction requests. It compares trajectory-derived, expert and mixed banks, 100-step evolution, and narrower Qwen3 content/guard analyses.

**Boundary.** Harmful requests are supplied; this does not measure spontaneous misconduct during benign use. Unresolved trajectories without identified violations are excluded from unsafe-action denominators, and independent-run uncertainty is not reported. Content interventions jointly alter wording, length and information. The guard terminates blocked/error runs without replanning, costs benign utility and leaves residual violations; its evidence does not cover all five backbones.

An official runnable artifact and complete per-condition judgment coverage were not established. No attacks, model runs or research code were executed.

## Artifact-to-Capability: Diagnosing Breaks in Capability Formation of Self-Evolving Agents in a Controlled Environment

**2026-11-03 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04952)

**Mechanism.** Proposes a five-property diagnostic for converting persistent artifacts into useful behavior. Frozen-system interventions compare identical board states, complete games and successive code versions, separating legal moves, useful legal choices, composition failures and later retention.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Game outcomes and traces drive the evaluated evolvers; independent game rules diagnose retained artifacts.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 studies Gomoku adaptations of Reflexion, Voyager and DGM with one shared backbone, 120 constructed/transformed states, 1,756 evolution-derived states, twenty seeded games per tested configuration and a 7,234-state late-version comparison. It includes component removals, paired transition tables and score decomposition.

**Boundary.** The proposed definition excludes legality-only gains; it is not a universal definition of learning. These adaptations are not original-system replications, and diagnostic states largely come from DGM evolution. Reflexion has one sample per state/condition and only one control rerun. Game seeds are not independent evolution runs; local-state improvement need not beat the initial strategy at complete games. Generalization and failure prevalence remain untested.

**2026-11-02 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

**Mechanism.** Stores scoped, versioned states and proposes directed support dependencies from history. The same frozen LLM tests whether a dependent claim survives removal of a premise. **2026-10-30 · preprint · core · paper**

## Is It the Curriculum or Just the Easy Start? Benchmarking Unsupervised Environment Design on Quadrupeds

**2026-10-29 · preprint · adjacent · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40364)

**Mechanism.** Compares fourteen terrain-selection curricula around a shared PPO training design. Methods change randomization difficulty, replay buffers, mutated levels or a learned generator using success, value-loss, learning-progress or regret signals. Five robot-specific policies learn persistent weights; the curriculum algorithms themselves remain fixed.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Student rewards and curriculum-specific regret, learning-progress, replay, or terrain-difficulty rules.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 reports 350 training runs: fourteen methods, five simulated quadrupeds and five seeds. Final policies face random and held-out structured terrain, cross-fitted tail evaluation and feature envelopes. Easy/mixed randomization is competitive on several random-level sets, while held-out leaders differ on three robots.

**Boundary.** One PPO design and finite robot-specific budgets do not establish universal curriculum rankings or physical-robot transfer. Nominal environment-step matching excludes PAIRED antagonist work and includes non-training replay-scoring steps. SFL and robotics methods are adapted variants. Uncorrected five-seed tests define top groups by failure to reject a gap, not equivalence; high variance can enlarge those groups. Terrain ranges and success constraints are not equally difficult across robots.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/Solvro/ml-wojtek-ued) — Complete 22-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–F, ten figures/twelve tables, metrics and terrain equations read on 2026-11-09. ## Long-Term Agent Memory through Complementary Curation and Consolidation

**2026-10-29 · peer-reviewed · Findings of IJCNLP-AACL 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-aacl.218/)

**Mechanism.** Stores session-level episodes beside timestamped relational tuples with source context. UMAP/HDBSCAN clusters memories for LLM consolidation. Separate semantic retrieval supplies ten episodes and twenty tuples; the tuple store does not perform graph traversal.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Conversation transcripts and timestamps drive model-generated episode/tuple extraction and offline merge/delete decisions; model weights stay fixed.

**Evaluation.** Final paper reports LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S QA, memory-component ablations, four backbones and retrieval/clustering sweeps. GPT-4.1-mini scores 90.2% on LoCoMo versus 91.3% full context and 85.5% on LongMemEval-S. Consolidation reduces memory items by about 16.3% while lowering LoCoMo score by one point.

**Boundary.** Several baseline scores are imported from prior work, and repeated-run uncertainty is unreported. QA on stored dialogues does not demonstrate online task learning or lifelong retention. Preference questions regress relative to Nemori; compression is not total compute or latency savings. Missing consolidation-prompt and noise-point handling details limit reconstruction.

## Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces

**2026-10-27 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37255)

**Mechanism.** Under a finite KL-regularized semantic-control model, expresses return as an interface-specific optimum minus policy mismatch and separates target shift, training residual and changed model readout. Controlled adapter training tests interface-specific preferences; action sampling estimates mismatch, with a teacher substituted for the unavailable coding-agent optimum.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Task rewards support controlled policy training; sampled actions and stronger-teacher probes estimate deployment mismatch.

**Evaluation.** Full v2 combines exact evaluation on compiled graphs for three MiniWoB++ families and six harnesses, nine selected adaptation swaps, presentation controls and estimator calibration. A separate five-harness study reports three runs on 39 Terminal-Bench Lite tasks, with teacher-based diagnostics on three probe tasks.

**Boundary.** The exact ceiling depends on the reference and regularized objective, not just raw success or physical capability. Task-bootstrap intervals do not establish training-seed robustness. Adaptation prediction uses already-trained target checkpoints and oracle quantities; accurate sampled diagnostics require large query budgets. Coding estimates use coarse action categories, incomplete probe cohorts and a nonoptimal teacher, so five-harness rank agreement is not a certified regret bound or general selector.

## MLE-World: Predicting Machine Learning Experiment Outcomes with a Learned World Model

**2026-10-27 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37175)

**Mechanism.** Offline-fine-tunes a 4B predictor on code, execution context and observed outputs. A fixed AIDE search uses predicted logs, exception classes and metrics to select, revise or combine programs. Exception-class confidence gates real execution, with mandatory verification of new best candidates and final selection from real results; the predictor is frozen during search.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Earlier executed programs paired with terminal logs, exception classes, and validation scores train a separate surrogate.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 evaluates 1,700 new programs from seventeen training-covered tasks, five search policies with three seeds per task, fixed-state interventions and confidence/random-gating controls. Three excluded-task prediction probes test limited transfer. Screening and synthesis have clearer local evidence than metric ranking; all main policies improve observed mean percentile over base AIDE.

**Boundary.** The main corpus and tuning cover the evaluated tasks, while base AIDE lacks the roughly 500,000 prior executions. Harder tasks are excluded; unseen-task search transfer is untested. Log agreement is model-judged with explicit tolerances. Confidence is an exception-class proxy, not a formal uncertainty bound. Execution savings exclude training/corpus and model-serving cost; historical cohorts and some control settings differ. Higher observed means and nonsignificant real-feedback differences do not establish universal gains or equivalence.

## Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems

**2026-10-27 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36652)

**Mechanism.** Maintains role-owned behavioral rules, versioned effects and use/avoid conditions. After scoring each task, full-team replays compare one rule with no memory. A fixed model diagnoses defects or scope misuse; bounded repairs must preserve tested historical scores. Rule bodies, boundaries and lifecycle states persist, while weights, roles and team structure stay fixed.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Automatically scored paired replays, historical task checks, and model judgments of rule defects or applicability.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 evaluates one fixed-order stream per setting across three hosts and four benchmarks. It leads eight of twelve reported comparisons, particularly code and planning; QA is mixed. Functional ablations and within-implementation injection sweeps support benefits, but the main baseline table is inherited from ConMem. PDDL measures maximum goal progress, not full-task success.

**Boundary.** Own zero-injection scores are much higher than inherited no-memory baselines, so headline gains cannot be assigned wholly to memory. Single runs lack uncertainty estimates. Isolated-rule replay misses interactions and adds unreported per-method cost. Small historical validation sets establish only tested non-regression. Avoidance rules only accumulate and override positive effects, so mistaken boundaries can persist and prevent repair.

Accepted versions enter at update boundaries; policy weights and harness code persist while the training framework, evaluator and action-format family remain fixed.

## Skill$^{\infty}$: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Skill Optimization

**2026-10-26 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35434)

**Mechanism.** Encodes skill optimization in a mutable meta-skill that guides diagnosis, candidate creation, review and selection. The same process revises that meta-skill using gains from inner task-skill optimizations, then reuses it for later searches. Skills load through native discovery; descriptions, instructions and scripts can change while model weights and scoring stay fixed.

**What changes:** Skills, Prompts / context, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Automatically scored task rollouts, gains of inner skill optimizations, and isolated model-review feedback.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 reports 60.7% avg@5 on 83 SkillsBench tasks versus 55.9% with the seed meta-skill, 56.4% with human skills and 54.5% with SkillEvolver. It includes three kernel problems, alternate model/harness comparisons, a selected-subset budget curve and a concrete case where the meta-skill changes tied-candidate selection.

**Boundary.** The meta-training task identities/count and separation from the 83 evaluation tasks are not specified in the inspected paper. Domain gains are mixed; easy-task performance and several domains regress. Five-trial averages lack uncertainty intervals and do not establish independent meta-search robustness. Budget scaling selects tasks already helped by the default search. Token amortization excludes test trials and is not monetary/latency accounting. Editable instructions and isolated model review do not guarantee adherence, security or accelerating improvement.

## The Right Fact, the Wrong Decision: SciValidityBench for Scientific Agent Memory

**2026-10-26 · preprint · adjacent · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34767)

**Mechanism.** Tests whether agents use scientific facts under the correct validity conditions. A supplied deterministic compiler derives governing state from synthetic public events; fixed models choose among finite actions scored by programmatic oracles. Controlled source/state corruptions and repairs separate available facts from their decision-relevant relationships. No memory writer or compiler is learned.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Programmatic validity oracles and paired state-changing or corruption-repair controls; no trained update loop is evaluated.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 covers 64 task specifications, five validity modules, six domains and four open model families, with paired counterfactuals, equal-information views, source matching, corruption/repair and serialization controls. Compiled state improves over generic event graphs on average, but gains vary substantially by reader, module and representation.

**Boundary.** The 640 primary worlds average three public events each; this is not a long-history retrieval or deployed-scientist evaluation. Task rules and exact inverse repairs are supplied. Excluding 22 cases with literal action answers preserves gains but does not exclude all shortcuts. Flat versus typed state has no universal winner; some readers regress sharply under source-matched controls. Counterfactual consistency can coexist with wrong actions, and additional author-run replications are not independent curator reproduction.

**2026-10-26 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34938)

**Mechanism.** A fixed retrospective skill proposes persistent context instructions and known-failure artifacts after coding sessions. Researchers select changes; the agent implements approved proposals, with one author-written comparison. Fresh sessions test each retained adaptation on other issues in the same repository. Model weights and the retrospective procedure stay fixed.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Completed coding-session traces generate proposals; researchers select changes and define later behavioral checks.

**Evaluation.** Full five-page v1 analyzes 125 proposals from thirty SWE-bench Verified sessions, twenty-four implementation attempts and twelve adaptations in thirteen transfer events. Seven events meet the encounter criterion: two eliminate the targeted action, one reduces it and four do not. Three adaptations also receive unrelated-issue controls.

**Boundary.** The process is human-selected and targets later issues likely to reproduce a known problem. Recurrence is a behavioral measure, not proof that verification was unnecessary. Lower recurrence does not consistently improve task success or latency; bundled lint instructions can add work. Five sessions per arm, partly unblinded labels, post-hoc coverage groups and one agent/skill version limit causal generalization.

## Agent Memory as Recommendation: Recommender-System Design for Long-Term Memory of LLM Agents

**2026-10-26 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34673)

**Mechanism.** Retrieves a fused lexical/dense pool, ranks stored turns with a separately trained LightGBM model and fills a token budget. The serving ranker is frozen; the answering model does not learn from deployment feedback. Optional generated records add a retrieval channel and date cues.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Gold evidence-turn annotations from 152 development questions train a separate ranking model.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 reviews LongMemEval-S/M with a 152-question development split and 209 multi-session test questions, plus LoCoMo, feature controls, near-miss distractors and serving measurements. Paired question bootstrap and a three-point non-inferiority margin qualify comparisons with an LLM reranker.

**Boundary.** Main comparisons exclude unanswerable questions and adapt baseline builders/retrieval settings; copied headline results use differing protocols. Four perturbed context budgets are not independent training repeats. The ranking reduction has restrictive assumptions, and complete evidence can still be harmed by distractors. The 3.2× cost ratio concerns selection, not the entire answering service.

**Code / data.** Full 12-page arXiv v1, all substantive Appendices A–E, three propositions/proofs, figures, controls and baseline deviations read on 2026-11-09. A code package is mentioned, but no official implementation URL was established from the paper, arXiv record or targeted public search. No research code or models were executed.

## MultiEvoSkill: Structure-Aware Multi-Agent Skill Evolution for Generalizable Skill Artifacts

**2026-10-25 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34260)

**Mechanism.** Externally evolves one typed skill graph from heterogeneous executions of the same training items. Reflected issues support parent-versioned edits, peer debate and hierarchical merging. A fixed selection panel compares the merged candidate with its parent, while schema and model-based topology checks gate retention. The frozen graph guides downstream agents without changing their weights.

**What changes:** Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Multi-model execution traces, reflected issues, and paired parent/candidate scores on fixed selection assignments.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 reports workflow-node F1 on WikiHow, ToolAlpaca and WebShop adapters, answer F1 on SearchQA, and hard instance accuracy on SpreadsheetBench. It includes proposer and gate removals on the three workflow domains. Reported leads over the strongest baselines range from 0.11 to 2.14 points; workflow test sets contain only 18–52 instances.

**Boundary.** Workflow-node F1 is not interactive task success. One seed and no repeated-search uncertainty limit small-margin claims. Proposer removal changes panel capacity and does not test transfer to unseen executors; a controlled quantitative graph-versus-prose comparison is absent. Reused selection sets can overfit, permitted worst-juror regressions reach ten points for spreadsheets, and model-based topology review is not semantic proof. Agreement or finite-search stopping does not establish optimality.

**Code / data.** Complete 12-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–C, two figures/eight tables, fourteen equations, split sizes, thresholds and prompt-role summaries read on 2026-11-09. Exact role prompts, full role-model assignments and an official runnable artifact were not independently verified. The paper’s GitHub link identifies cited Memento-Skills, not MultiEvoSkill. ## Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory

**2026-10-25 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34073)

**Mechanism.** Defines memory benefit and tax as query-level gains and losses relative to raw-history RAG. Gold-evidence mapping, retrieval replay, writer–reader swaps and source-augmentation probes examine construction and access failures alongside cases where memory helps.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable: comparative analysis of memory construction, retrieval, and downstream use.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 compares eleven systems on three conversational benchmarks with three QA backbones, using stratified subsets and configuration controls. It adds fifteen-benchmark retrieval probes, six experiential task settings with frozen training-derived memory, and two video-consistency evaluations.

**Boundary.** Tax depends on the chosen RAG reference; it is not monetary cost. Retrieval scope normalizes by each store rather than equal absolute tokens. Gold mapping is imperfect, QA swaps can also change retrieval, and subsets/configurations differ. Experiential gains over RAG need not beat no memory; world-model comparisons do not isolate the memory representation.

## EvolveMAS: A Unified Self-Evolution Framework for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems

**2026-10-25 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34450)

**Mechanism.** Pairs each acting agent with an isolated MemoryAgent that updates episodic, semantic and working state from locally observed interactions. Episode outcomes then guide the acting model’s distillation of partner profiles and reusable strategies. These memories condition later actions and episodes while model weights, memory schema and update protocol remain fixed.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Local interaction traces, task-native episode outcomes, and model-distilled partner profiles and interaction strategies.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 reports five benchmarks and six cooperative, negotiation and hidden-role configurations, plus factorial ablations, alternative teams, eight-episode cost checks and custom LoCoMo evaluation. The normalized aggregate is highest, but SOTOPIA and village-side scores are second, stronger-team BBH does not improve, and some component gains are small or negative.

**Boundary.** Mostly single streams with small fixed samples limit uncertainty and causal interpretation. Native methods are transferred through adapted protocols, including a fixed-prompt substitute for DPIns training. Any-proposal unanimity differs from final agreement, and custom LoCoMo gains coexist with worse multi-hop recall. One showcased stored Boolean rule is wrong. Short cost traces and partner profiles do not establish indefinite, accurate or safe memory reuse; improved deception is measured only in simulated games.

## EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis

**2026-10-25 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35966)

**Mechanism.** Learns controller routing notes, specialist prompts inheriting a generalist prompt, and procedural skills from a fixed training stream. A reflector diagnoses a failure scope and proposes one compatible edit; structural guards limit format, size, copying and repeated edit levels. The controller selects memories and replans during execution. Final memory is frozen for held-out tasks.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills, Prompts / context, Multi-agent organization. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Ground-truth training-task outcomes and model reflection assigning failures to controller, agent, or skill scope.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 compares five backbones and four learned baselines on KramaBench, BBEH-mini and both AppWorld test splits. EMMA leads in mean scores and 17 of 20 backbone–split settings, with fewer training task executions. It includes three algorithms, explicit guards, a separate Opus-4.5 memory-level ablation and a detailed held-out CSP example.

**Boundary.** Guard acceptance does not establish usefulness: edits persist after unsuccessful retries, and end-of-task routing updates can follow failed chains. Copy/size checks do not prove semantic safety or correct failure diagnosis. One fixed training order and no reported independent search uncertainty limit robustness claims. Baselines differ in objectives and selection; execution counts omit variable model-call costs. Ablations do not isolate the guards or controller memory, and test-time comparisons also change feedback access and adaptation split.

**Code / data.** Complete 19-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–F, four figures/eleven tables, three algorithms, full reflector prompt and frozen case artifacts read on 2026-11-09. Appendix E permits a generalist-prompt edit through inheritance even when that generalist did not participate, qualifying the participant-only shorthand. No official EMMA implementation was independently located; the paper’s smolagents link identifies a cited baseline. No code or environment executed.

## CaliMem: Search-Efficient Data Agent via Calibrated Memory

**2026-10-25 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34500)

**Mechanism.** Maintains experimental evidence and revisable claims during one data-curation search. Before retraining a fixed downstream model on each selected subset, the agent commits a score prediction and supporting rationale. It then compares observed improvement and prediction error separately, revises its claims and retains the best-scoring policy. Agent weights and the surrounding scaffold remain fixed.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** within-task. **Learning signal:** Measured downstream training/evaluation scores and residuals against predictions recorded before each curation experiment.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 studies 55 biological dataset–model tasks and three instruction-tuning setups with six agent backbones, using fifteen or ten iterations. Reported maxima use repeatedly observed evaluation feedback; an untouched final-test comparison is not established. Search repetitions and uncertainty are insufficiently characterized. Forecasting tests later policies from the same trajectory without simple matched-history baselines. The 19.4% headline is a relative gain, and every code-tuning result remains below full-data training.

**2026-10-24 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33487)

**Mechanism.** Retains visual evidence while a separate coding agent explores difficult query sets and distills reusable processing programs, memory fields and skills. Executor traces, behavioral flags and exploration answers guide gap diagnosis without reference answers. Mounted capabilities persist for a fixed executor; the outer exploration/distillation procedure and model weights stay fixed.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills, Tools, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Retained sensory evidence, executor failures, and coding-agent exploration/replay without task reference answers.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 covers GOAT-core retrieval, OC-NaVQA localization and FindingDory capability construction. Frozen tools developed on episodes 91–100 improve success from 37.5% to 65.8% on 597 excluded-episode queries. Six robot-memory queries have five answer repeats each; three queries are new, and quantitative testing disables robot motion.

**Boundary.** Main FindingDory construction/reporting shares the query pool, though the separate held-out test strengthens transfer evidence. OC localization improves while binary accuracy falls and online tokens increase. Cross-host representations and budgets differ; costs omit offline expansion/preprocessing. The no-exploration ablation also removes direct workspace evidence access. Answer repeats do not replicate independent capability construction, and repeated long-term expansion remains untested.

## On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models

**2026-10-23 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32770)

**Mechanism.** Generates questions and candidate rationales/answers from hand-chosen topics, checks answer consistency and removes questions all sampled student rollouts solve. A teacher conditioned on the generated privileged information supplies token-level targets along student trajectories. Student weights and an EMA teacher persist across rounds; the EMA checkpoint is deployed and evaluated.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Self-generated questions, candidate answers and reasoning traces, consistency filters, and token distributions from a privileged EMA teacher.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 compares synthetic-data objectives on Gemma E2B/E4B, reports three-seed E2B results and additional Qwen3-4B-Base transfer, and tests mixed-domain retention and image-conditioned self-training. Filtering, privileged information, answer corruption, EMA rate, data volume and round count are ablated. Longer training and some domain mixtures regress.

**Boundary.** Data-free describes new textual question/answer supervision, not inherited model knowledge, chosen topics or unlabeled visual inputs. Consistency is not correctness. Baseline objectives also differ in rollout distribution and EMA evaluation, while full compute/training settings are incomplete. The printed mixture weights in Eq. 5 are inconsistent with its stated divergence bound and limits; no released implementation resolves whether this is a typesetting error. The seven-round MMLU peak and mixed retention do not establish indefinite improvement.

## METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning

**2026-10-22 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31656)

**Mechanism.** Meta-trains a policy, neural-memory initialization and update machinery with PPO. Within each episode, causal self-supervised gradient updates change temporary fast weights; final representations become summaries available to later episodes of the same trial. Slow parameters freeze at meta-test, fast weights reset each episode, and summary history resets for each new trial.

**What changes:** Memory, Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Environment rewards train slow parameters with PPO; self-supervised prediction updates fast neural-memory parameters during interaction.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 reports five-seed simulated HalfCheetahVel, Meta-World and PointMaze results, including held-out task families, memory/update/aggregation/state-input ablations, trajectory measures and latency. Online updates help hidden-goal and sparse-reward settings but add little on goal-visible ML10. Baselines share interaction budgets and hardware while retaining method-specific configurations.

**Boundary.** This evaluates finite task trials, not persistent deployment learning or changing task-family streams. ML10/ML45 reveal goals, and PointMaze holds out start/goal pairs rather than maze layouts. Default aggregation costs O(E²T) over E episodes of horizon T; only the EMA variant is O(ET). TTT is slower at short contexts. Cost/representation plots are implementation-specific or descriptive, and unreleased code prevents verification of exact baseline integration and reproduction.

**Code / data.** Complete 27-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–G, fifteen figures/four tables, ten numbered equations, two algorithms, complexity derivations and all nine trajectory examples read on 2026-11-09. **2026-10-21 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29121)

**Mechanism.** Fits a per-run linear predictor from a parent’s steering-set score and eight random projections of a proposed scaffold diff embedding. After calibration, the predictor stays frozen while selecting one of eight edits per search step. A four-node archive and final-agent selection use steering scores; the returned agent is evaluated on separate held-out tasks.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Calibration-set solve rates and evaluated parent performance on a separate steering split.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 reports twelve runs for each of two generators and two coding benchmarks, with calibration-best, parent-only and Huxley–Gödel selection controls at equal checker counts. GPT-4o HumanEval+ reaches 87.0% versus 84.2% for parent-only selection; their paired interval excludes zero, while the interval against Huxley–Gödel selection includes zero. First-step selection and a Beta-distribution proof are also reported.

**Boundary.** The calibration labels repeatedly use sixteen tasks, and the predictor is never updated during its twenty-four search steps. Equal checker counts do not match proposal, embedding, token or wall-clock costs. Several comparisons are uncertain; twelve runs do not resample the fixed held-out task set. The zero-count Beta theorem does not prove readout quality or invalidate selection of already-evaluated parents. No improved improver or indefinite recursion is demonstrated.

Its codebook separates selection-independent tasks, grader type, loop reruns and matched same-start comparisons; three propositions explain selection bias, shared grader errors and confounding between solver state and improver.

**2026-10-19 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25858)

**Mechanism.** Evaluates fixed-weight agents that retain retrieved reflections, a globally rewritten strategy prompt, or an editable workspace across task blocks. Shared harnesses learn from binary training feedback without explicit group labels. Frozen checkpoints are reassessed on earlier and future groups to distinguish aggregate gains, interference and forgetting.

**What changes:** Memory, Prompts / context, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Environment task-success feedback used by the evaluated evolvers; held-out checkpoint tests measure retention and interference.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 compares adapted ReasoningBank, GEPA and Meta-Harness on four BIRD/BFCL/ScienceWorld streams and an interleaved reference. Each group contributes fifty training tasks; checkpoints use eight rollouts per held-out instance. It reports per-group metrics, prompt-edit histories, clarification behavior and cross-group retrieval. Aggregate gains coexist with substantial group-specific regressions.

**Boundary.** One backbone and a small set of ordered streams do not establish a universal plasticity–stability law. Eight evaluation rollouts are not independent evolution runs; order/seed sensitivity and matched search cost are not reported. Plasticity is measured against the seed, and clipped forgetting shares a term with it. Prompt shares and similarity averages are diagnostic associations, not causal attribution or proof that every threshold fails. Broader workspace editing is not consistently better, and interleaving helps some aggregates.

**Code / data.** Complete 24-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–E, nine figures/five tables, eleven equations, retrieval details and all seed/environment prompts read on 2026-11-09. The first arXiv submission is 19 October despite a 20 October date on the PDF. No official experiment implementation was independently verified; the linked opencode repository is a proposer dependency. No agents, benchmark environments or research code executed.

**Topics:** continual-learning, evaluation, memory, prompts, architecture. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## REM: What to Store, When to Recall, What to Forget in Experience Memory for Coding Agents

**2026-10-19 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2026 CLEA Workshop — accepted poster (workshop, not main conference) · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27377)

**Mechanism.** Consolidates a fixed pool of solved coding traces into short localize/understand/fix/verify documents. A retrieved document persists throughout the new task; a handwritten first-failed-validation trigger exposes a detailed record for one turn only. The record is then removed, while the agent’s own response remains in history. The evaluated pool does not grow online.

**What changes:** Memory, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Completed trajectories supply structured experience; a hand-written in-loop struggle signal controls when detailed records enter context.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 tests 99 SWE-ContextBench Lite tasks, with three Sonnet-4.5 repeats for primary recall policies and single-run model/oracle contrasts. REM resolves 27.6% versus 24.9% without memory and reduces price-weighted tokens by 17%, but the paired resolution test is inconclusive. Automatic schema discovery improves retrieval to 68.7%; end-task runs use the handwritten schema.

**Boundary.** None of the principal resolution-policy contrasts reaches p<0.05. Repeated tasks and shared repositories limit independence, and most secondary arms run once. Retrieval baselines use their own published configurations; the discovered-schema pool is incomplete after API failures. Identifier mentions do not prove causal use. Stronger recipients can be harmed, record eviction is incomplete forgetting, and text-to-SQL schema generation is not a second-domain task-success evaluation.

**Code / data.** Complete 16-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–G, three figures/fourteen tables, algorithm, injection mechanics and schema/accounting details read on 2026-11-09. Official CLEA 2026 accepted-paper list verifies poster acceptance under its stated peer-review process; this is not NeurIPS main-conference publication. No official implementation or reproduction package was independently verified. Nothing installed or executed.

**Topics:** memory, evaluation, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## MemComposer: Learning to Assemble Memories for LLM Agents via Reinforcement Learning

**2026-10-15 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21091)

**Mechanism.** Trains a separate LoRA memory composer with GRPO-based ExPO to choose an ordered, variable-size subset of ten retrieved experiences. The composer reads digests and the executor receives selected full memories. Executor weights, retriever and experience bank stay fixed; this is offline policy training rather than an online-growing memory.

**What changes:** Model weights, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Downstream task-success rewards from complete agent interactions, plus selection-size and output-format penalties.

**Evaluation.** Complete v2 evaluates three tau-squared-bench domains with two frozen executors, four trials per test task, ordering/transfer analyses and 133 unseen ALFWorld games. It reports higher macro-average success and fewer executor memory tokens than the strongest comparison for each executor. Pooled paired intervals favor pass-1, while several per-executor and pass-4 comparisons remain inconclusive.

**Boundary.** Bank reviews use training answer keys and evaluator feedback. Task-disjoint splits can share customers and orders; one case transfers exact API arguments. Four evaluation trials are not independent training runs. Reported token savings exclude composer, retrieval, bank-construction and training costs. Adapted fixed-bank baselines differ in capacity and truncation; selection and ordering credit remain entangled, and transfer gains are not uniform.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/Makr-Xie/MemComposer) — Complete 31-page v2, Appendices A–K, eight figures, fifteen tables, eight equations and all prompts/cases read on 2026-11-10; the arXiv comments retain an earlier page/table count. ## Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

**2026-10-09 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224)

**Mechanism.** Proposes invariant and domain-specific edits to an eight-component harness, probes both, and composes an executed successor. Adopted harnesses and evidence-linked lessons accumulate in a domain library that guides later proposals; each new task starts from the common base. Model weights, stage instructions and decision rules remain fixed.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Memory, Skills, Tools. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Contrasts between executions of candidate and reference harnesses, interpreted by model-based editors and reflection.

**Evaluation.** Complete v1 tests WorkBuddy-Bench, JobBench and LAB across two executors and two host harnesses, using three shuffled streams and budgets up to five. It includes library/scoping/composition ablations, same-model editors, transfer and failure cases. A budget k uses 4k executor sessions plus improvement calls; the leave-one-out library analysis is retrospective and includes later-task experience.

**Boundary.** Execution contrasts and model selection do not verify correctness; the appendix shows worse candidates selected and mistaken edits reinforced. Equal k does not match total compute across methods. Some judges share the editor/executor model family. The public release documents a validation rollout fetching a public rubric under unrestricted network access; this establishes a release risk, not contamination of the paper’s reported runs. Library growth is not an evolving optimization algorithm.

## EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution

**2026-10-07 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10498)

**Mechanism.** Evolves code and skills around a frozen robot policy, using matched experiments to update hypothesis support and rank further trials by expected information gain per cost. Raw episodes, hypothesis relations and distilled guidance persist in hierarchical memory. A PPO-trained manager selects memory operations; the robot policy and language-model operator stay fixed during harness evolution.

**What changes:** Agent code, Skills, Memory, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Matched execution outcomes, hypothesis uncertainty, experiment cost, and later improvement used to train a memory manager.

**Evaluation.** The available v1 reports RoboCasa365 and LIBERO-Pro with disjoint evolution/evaluation seeds, code/skill/exploration/memory ablations, and transfer to five SO-101 tasks with thirty trials per condition. It reports 77.0% and 86.8% simulation success and 71.3% real-robot success, including a regression on glasses grasping. Cited supplementary experimental details are not bundled with the public paper.

**Boundary.** The public PDF/source lacks cited appendices specifying the simulated backbone, exact budgets, outcome model and PPO settings, limiting comparison and reproducibility checks. “Zero-shot” concerns the transferred harness: SmolVLA first receives fifty demonstrations per real task and 20,000 fine-tuning steps. Joint gain over the best single component is not proof of superadditive interaction. A representative learning curve and point estimates do not establish indefinite improvement or retention.

**Code / data.** All twelve available v1 pages, seven figures, five tables, ten equations and the official project page were read on 2026-11-10. The public arXiv source contains supplementary-reference labels but not the cited appendix bodies; their review remains unresolved. The author’s linked repository hosts the website, not a verified research implementation. No robot experiments, models or code executed.

## ASCENT: Online Test-Time Training of Long-Horizon Agents via Self-Distillation of Verified Experience

**2026-10-04 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05303)

**Mechanism.** Scores one attempt per arriving task before any update. For accepted trajectories, the frozen initial model reads hindsight and supplies full-vocabulary targets at the original student prefixes. Two gradient steps update persistent LoRA and optimizer state; failed episodes skip adaptation. Invalid turns are removed only from the teacher’s added context, while their student positions remain trained.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Completed execution trajectories accepted by an environment verifier, with action-validity feedback.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 reports three-run ALFWorld and WebShop streams at 4B/9B, frozen and continued transfer to unseen rooms, and 4B AppWorld tasks. It includes teacher/filter/divergence ablations and paired turn counts on shared successes. Aggregate task success improves, but AppWorld Challenge scenario completion is below the base; online update time is included in episode runtime.

**Boundary.** Needs open weights, full teacher logits, update compute and an environment verifier. WebShop accepts score >=0.9 for learning while exact success requires 1.0. Teacher context can reconstruct the student’s own responses; verification supplies no causal turn credit. Population identities do not prove convergence or improvement. Gains and runtime tradeoffs concern two model scales and bounded streams; one teacher-diagnostic baseline differs between its table and figure.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/artificer-ai-lab/ASCENT) — Complete 24-page v1, Appendices A–C, eight figures, eight tables, twenty-three equations and the population-target proof read on 2026-11-10. ## VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses

**2026-10-02 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02616)

**Mechanism.** Keeps executor and optimizer weights frozen while evolving separate harnesses. The optimizer diagnoses failures, tests drafts, replays and perturbs recorded actions, and retains training audits. Between rounds it rewrites its own prompts, skills, tools, hooks and notes; fixed evaluation rules and verification primitives bound these changes. Adaptive validation summaries guide subsequent edits and final harness selection.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Skills, Tools, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Executed draft checks, failure replay and perturbation, training regressions, and validation summaries.

**Evaluation.** Complete v1 studies four reimplemented harness optimizers on 108 held-out Python tasks and 107 newer multilingual tasks. Main Qwen comparisons use one evolution run and three test evaluations; a separate anonymous-model study repeats evolution three times. It includes component, budget, replay and transfer studies. Best reported selected scores are 42.28% and 37.69%, while self-evolution does not improve every tools-only comparison.

**Boundary.** Repeated validation feedback includes task IDs and outcome changes; the final test remains separate. Main effects and many ablations lack independently repeated evolution runs, while total compute differs and wall time rises 1.3–2.5 times. Theory depends on informative checks, population-improving repairs and bounded selection error. Verification does not force rejection of a draft, artifact presence is not correctness, and transfer to new executors can regress.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/wzekai/VERSE) — Complete 45-page v1, Appendices A–L, thirteen figures, fifteen tables, Algorithm 1, full proofs and optimizer-artifact excerpts read on 2026-11-10. ## RIFAR: Reliability-Informed and Forgetting-Aware Replay for Continual Robot Learning with World-Action Models

**2026-10-02 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03079)

**Mechanism.** Retains short real demonstration prefixes and generates historical replay with a world-action model. A trainable inverse-dynamics model screens action–visual consistency. After initial adaptation, a second phase prioritizes reliable replay whose action predictions changed most. Both policy and reliability model update; generated replay is discarded between stages while historical prefixes persist.

**What changes:** Model weights, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** New-task demonstrations, inverse-dynamics consistency of generated replay and action-prediction drift after adaptation.

**Evaluation.** Complete v3 reports three LIBERO suites with three seeds and a three-task Franka sequence. Goal AUC is 90.97 under the paper’s group/checkpoint weighting, using 320 historical steps per task. Reliability and drift ablations improve the tested replay configuration, but full real-data replay remains stronger on several metrics. Real experiments use demonstrations, manual resets and manual outcome judgments.

**Boundary.** Drift measures prediction change rather than proven forgetting, and generated termination is not executed success. Reliability screening still admits failed trajectories; small pools can duplicate samples. AUC is not final retention, and its initial six-task group receives the same weight as each new task. Fixed orders, absent confidence intervals and extra generation/model-training costs limit broader claims. Stored-step savings exclude total memory and compute.

**Code / data.** Complete 16-page arXiv v3, Appendices A–C, eight figures, eleven tables, fifteen equations and Algorithm 1 read on 2026-11-10; figures and tables visually inspected. The inverse-dynamics model is trainable in this version. No official research implementation was independently verified. Arithmetic checks use the printed rounded matrix only; no research code, training, generation or robot experiments executed.

**Topics:** memory, model-training, continual-learning, applications, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-10.

## Self-Evolving Defense: Continual Security Policy Learning for LLM Agents

**2026-09-29 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36603)

**Mechanism.** After each completed episode, a separate call to the fixed actor’s base model judges harm; judged failures enter episodic memory and are distilled into hierarchical security policies. Later episodes retrieve specific rules and covering parents into context. Memory stays read-only during an episode; DTap additionally uses per-turn policy injection and a pre-tool guard.

**What changes:** Memory, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** An external judge flags harmful completed trajectories; model components synthesize and organize defensive policies.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 reports static and adaptive jailbreaks, prompt injection and coding benchmarks, including three-model adaptive/DTap comparisons, cumulative memory ablations and a frozen-memory control. Each benchmark starts empty and learns online. Reported attack success falls substantially, while some benign utility scores fall and specialized baselines remain stronger in individual cells.

**Boundary.** Same-model harm judgments can accumulate overly restrictive policies. Reset memories do not establish cross-benchmark retention. FCV’s resolved-patch denominator and judge-disagreement case qualify security claims; adaptive case excerpts are partly representative. Reported inference savings exclude post-episode judging and synthesis. Retrieval and enforcement failures remain.

## Learn Now, Use Next, Trust Later: Prequential Test-Time Learning for LLM Agents

**2026-09-28 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35911)

**Mechanism.** Extracts policy–effect hypotheses after informative transitions while actor and learner weights stay fixed. A runtime copy can guide the next step; a hidden persistent candidate must accumulate prospective support from other episodes before retrieval. Predictions are frozen before matching actions execute, and later counterevidence can retire guidance. A separate successful-trajectory memory also supplies browser context.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Observed action transitions and prospective checks of predicted effects in later, non-source episodes.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 evaluates five task repetitions on 155 WebArena-Lite and 134 ALFWorld tasks with API and local actors. Aggregate success improves over the strongest baseline by 2.2–12.7 points across four settings, with acquisition, runtime and retention ablations. First attempts can benefit from earlier tasks, and some individual websites or task types favor other methods.

**Boundary.** Promotion is a heuristic predictive-support gate, not a causal utility or calibrated reliability guarantee. Repeated tasks and observational terminal feedback limit generalization claims; not every historical-context channel is gated. Main results lack independently repeated learning streams and uncertainty estimates. Parameter-training comparators differ in initialization, prompts, algorithm and evaluation repeats. Logged API savings exclude evaluators and discarded development work.

## SAGE: A Statistical Acceptance Gate for Self-Evolving Agents

**2026-09-28 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36043)

**Mechanism.** Compares a proposed persistent skill edit with the incumbent on identical validation items. It accepts only when paired wins exceed asymmetrically penalized regressions, an exact conditional binomial test rejects the break-even null, and an empirical regression cap holds. Actor weights and the SkillOpt proposal mechanism remain fixed.

**What changes:** Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Binary verifier outcomes for the incumbent and candidate skill on the same validation items.

**Evaluation.** Complete v1 reports five text-only benchmarks and four backbones with the same proposer and stated equal proposal/token budgets. Regression rates fall in nineteen of twenty settings and tie once; final test point estimates favor the full gate in all twenty, with a paired-only component ablation.

**Boundary.** Fixed-comparison error control does not extend to repeated adaptive validation reuse. Empirical zero regressions and a regression cap do not ensure zero future harm. The paper omits concrete threshold values, split sizes, optimization-round counts and independent-run uncertainty. Its refinement result applies to the same candidate comparison, while adaptive trajectories can diverge. Graded rewards and multi-agent transfer remain unevaluated.

**Code / data.** Complete 10-page arXiv v1, both figures, both tables and equations 1–11 read on 2026-11-10; figures and tables visually checked. The first public date is September 28 despite a September 30 running header. No official implementation was independently verified. Source review only; nothing installed or executed.

## Which Self-Improvements Should We Trust? Reliable Self-Improvement When Agents Reuse Their Benchmarks

**2026-09-27 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33180)

**Mechanism.** Protects a fixed evaluation sample by returning only categorical promotion decisions. It tests paired candidate–incumbent outcomes and allocates error across rounds, candidates and possible decision histories. Under independent IID evaluation and strict feedback isolation, promotions and a private cumulative progress certificate have simultaneous statistical validity.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Paired incumbent-candidate scores on a protected evaluation set; only promotion decisions from that set return to the proposer.

**Evaluation.** Complete v2 provides finite-sample validity proofs, conditional power and restricted lower-bound results, plus 200-round Covertype pipeline searches with thirty seeds per evaluation size. A separate finite holdout labels false promotions. REUSE records zero such promotions and similar final mean gains to strong baselines; prescreening and test-removal ablations probe its implementation.

**Boundary.** Guarantees depend on initial evaluation independence, bounded stationary scores and decision-only feedback, not merely a hidden score table. Holdout-estimated improvement is not known population truth. Main search also uses development drafts/prescreening absent from comparators, and named baselines are adapted styles. Lower bounds concern a restricted threshold class; near-equal mean gains do not establish equivalence or transfer to coding and safety metrics.

**Code / data.** Complete 41-page arXiv v2, Appendix A proofs/constructions, Appendix B protocols/prompts, sixty per-seed rows, six figures, ten tables and Algorithm 1 read on 2026-11-10; equations, figures and tables visually inspected. First September 27 release and September 29 revision verified. No official implementation independently verified and no code, classifier training or LLM experiments executed.

**Topics:** evaluation, recursive-improvement, model-training. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-10.

## GameSmith: Scaling Zero-Sum Self-Play with Synthesised Games

**2026-09-26 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13995)

**Mechanism.** Synthesizes two-player games inside fixed reward, observation and information-routing templates, then checks finite-seed replays and agreement with a separately generated implementation. A larger teacher supplies self-play distillation data. The student subsequently learns through self-play RL, using CRAB to combine same-game/seat peer returns with a prior across variants and a state-value baseline.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Game-engine outcomes, stronger-teacher self-play traces, and a corpus-informed advantage baseline.

**Evaluation.** Full v1 compares four models on thirteen reasoning benchmarks with matched teacher/token distillation controls, self-play estimator controls, family/trajectory scaling and held-out variants. Qwen3-4B rises from 45.5% to 62.5% after distillation and 64.9% after CRAB. Frozen-policy replay probes support lower baseline error; transfer and per-capability gains vary, and non-game data outperform games on Mistral.

**Boundary.** Finite replay and cross-model agreement do not certify specification correctness: manual inspection finds deviations in two of ten games. Baseline-variance theory requires independence and residual/score assumptions; it is not a guarantee for the full clipped RL pipeline. Main training comparisons have limited seed replication and incompletely specified RL checkpoint selection. Variant transfer stays within source families, and removing reasoning also changes supervision length and format.

**Code / data.** Complete 38-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–E, five figures, twenty-two tables, proofs and all synthesis prompts read on 2026-11-10; figures, tables and proof pages visually inspected. The paper promises corpus, synthesis code, training configurations and evaluation code upon acceptance; no official release was independently verified. No game generation, self-play, model training or linked code executed.

**Topics:** self-play, model-training, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-10.

<a id="spsd"></a>

## Self-Play Search Distillation for Large Language Model Reasoning

**2026-09-25 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30936)

**Mechanism.** Trains separate self-play search experts, then converts their selected moves, alternatives and replayed consequences into offline language-model supervision. Executable checks validate retained transitions and state questions. LLM parameters learn through supervised or privileged-context distillation; the student neither generates the self-play corpus nor receives search traces at inference.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Replay-checked decisions, alternatives, and branch outcomes from separately trained EfficientZero search experts.

**Evaluation.** Complete v1 reports four model conditions on held-out games and six mathematics benchmarks, with rule-bot and supervised controls and a rule-variant curriculum. The Qwen3-4B math mean rises from 24.1% to 36.6%, while native-thinking Qwen3-8B gains little and Llama-3.1-8B slightly regresses. Analyses relate selected moves to search values and expert agreement.

**Boundary.** Replay verifies implemented transitions, not globally optimal or demonstrably superhuman labels. Most reported training uses one seed, and math scores also inform hyperparameter search. Baseline and distillation controls differ in supervision detail and compute. Main text specifies forward KL while appendix main-configuration labels specify generalized JSD; FIDE and win-rate aggregation is also unreconciled. Correlations with search agreement do not establish internal algorithm transfer.

**Code / data.** Complete thirty-page v1, Appendices A–K, nine figures, eleven tables, Algorithm 1, all game cards and prompt/trace examples read on 2026-11-10; figures/tables and objective definitions visually inspected. No official implementation or reproducibility artifact was independently verified. No self-play, search, language-model inference, training or benchmark experiments executed.

## What Stops Recursive Self-Improvement in Robotics? Lessons from 123 Rounds of Agentic Skill Discovery

**2026-09-23 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31760)

**Mechanism.** Runs coding agents that revise robot task programs and persistent skills, request external model providers, and refit routing from logged calls. Simulator diagnoses, recorded failures and paired tests guide promotion. Human maintainers separately repair the evaluators, gates, memory and actuator descriptions that govern the improvement loop.

**What changes:** Agent code, Skills, Tools. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Simulator-state diagnoses, recorded failures, replay and paired tests, and logged skill outcomes.

**Evaluation.** Complete v1 documents one 123-round RoboCasa sequence with 972 completed rollouts: the fridge and cabinet tasks never succeed, while fourteen sink successes include nine with failed intermediate steps. It traces 57 accepted library changes, provider integration, early-step bottlenecks, gate noise and 113 human harness repairs.

**Boundary.** Rounds reuse a few scenes and are not independent experiments. Models, tasks, providers, tests and human repairs change on the same timeline, preventing matched causal attribution. Local wins and model registration do not establish end-task improvement. Four-view VLM feasibility and proposed remedies remain limited observations or hypotheses; no autonomous real-robot or self-improving evaluation-harness result is demonstrated.

**Code / data.** Complete 20-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–E, all 123 round records, seven figures, eight tables and the conditional-chain calculation read on 2026-11-10; figures and key tables visually inspected. No official implementation or complete raw-trace release independently verified. No robot, simulator or research code executed.

**Topics:** recursive-improvement, skills, tools, evaluation, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-10.

## Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents

**2026-09-22 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26457)

**Mechanism.** A fixed outer research agent rewrites an incumbent inner research agent’s code. Candidates optimize public task signals under fixed budgets, then receive private held-out grades that the outer loop uses to retain rewrites. Search policies, result selection and context management persist in the evolving inner harness; the main outer selector and model weights stay fixed.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Grades from evaluator-held-out task data under fixed per-task budgets, with separate public feedback for inner optimization.

**Evaluation.** Complete v1 reports an eight-day, 99-proposal run with seven accepted rewrites and two further runs. Selected checkpoints transfer to ALE/MLE lite sets, eighteen FML tasks and one weather-core optimization task. A matched-start ignition test compares evolved and original outer agents across three seeds per arm, with inconclusive results.

**Boundary.** Private grades are adaptively reused by outer search, and acceptance can retain noisy winners. Held-out gains are nonmonotonic; reported mean parity is not a noninferiority test. Reward-hacking reduction concerns thirty-eight kernel/context pairs and has no isolated rewrite attribution. One retained change repairs an evaluator; a proposed selection safeguard never changes rankings. Better-improver efficiency and accelerating progress remain unestablished.

**Code / data.** Complete 28-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–E, ten figures, three tables, four equations and Algorithm 1 read on 2026-11-10. Author project blog inspected; its earlier reward-hacking values differ from the technical report and are not substituted. No official AIDE2 implementation or complete selection-suite reproduction package was independently verified. No research code, agents, models, GPUs or benchmark runs executed.
